page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left margin holds marginal notes ("Cafus 38", "a Rom.14.", "14."). The right margin is cut off at the scan edge; its fragments are not legible and are described under notes. Running head centred above the text, page number at the top left.

main_text.l: æstimationem juris-jurandi, & præcep-
tum Christi de non jurando violare, &
fratri offendiculum præbere, & semet
perjurii periculo exponere.
SECT. IX.
Quartum & ultimum dignoscendi Ju-
ramenti κριτήριον[?] est mens & Intentio ju-
rantis. Esto enim non constet vel ex ver-
bis ipsis, vel ex communi æstimatione
hominum, aliquam sermonis formulam
esse Juramentum: Siquis tamen ejusmo-
di formula usus, aut mentis suæ errore[?]
aliquo putet se jurasse, aut ex aliqua do-
losa intentione velit putari jurasse; ea
formula etsi non sit revera & ex se jura-
mentum, habebit tamen quoad ipsum
hominem, ad omnem obligandi effe-
ctum in conscientia Juramenti instar, i-
ta ut non modo mendacii, sed & per-
jurii reus sit in foro interno, si fidem sibi
datam violaverit. Ut enim judice Apo-
stolo, qui æstimat aliquid esse
κοινόν[?] quod ex se non
est κοινόν, est illi tamen κοινόν[?], ita ut ab eo
teneatur abstinere sicut à re verè commu-
ni & impura: Sic a lege contrariorum
qui aliquid æstimat esse ἅγιον[?], id est sa

page.notes: Right margin: cropped at the scan edge; only word fragments remain and cannot be read, so no right-hand notes are transcribed. Greek words marked [?] are partly cut or faint in the scan: κριτήριον, the first κοινόν, the second κοινόν, ἅγιον. "errore" is faint at the line end and marked [?]. Catchword "crum" completes "sacrum", which is split across the page end; the main text ends on "sa". Long s is rendered as s throughout (printed "fi" and "fe" forms read as "si" and "se"). Printed "Iuramentum" and "Iuramenti" are given with J, as in the book's own "Jurisjurandi".
